transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... well, it's the voices, really. I keep hearing people talking about me. Usually it's through the conference room walls, or even coming from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's the board members, mostly, or some of the senior staff, and they're just going on and on about how I'm ruining the company. It sounds so incredibly clear that I actually catch myself answering them out loud before I realize no one else in the room heard a thing. 

It's just like that time we were trying to launch the new software integration, you know? We had this massive vendor dispute, and the lead developer—who, by the way, always wore these absolutely hideous neon green sneakers to every single executive meeting—he just completely stopped responding to my emails. I mean, who does that when you're on a multi-million dollar deadline? I ended up having to drive all the way down to the server farm in the middle of the night just to get someone to look at the deployment logs. And the traffic on the interstate was just unbelievable for a Tuesday at 2 AM. I don't even know where all those trucks were going. Anyway, yes, the voices about the company. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been hearing these voices and having these experiences—days, weeks, or longer?

Let's see... the voices from the walls, and the ones coming through my phone, it's been happening for about the past three months now. Right around the time we were doing the Q2 financial review. 

Which, honestly, was a complete nightmare because our caterer for the board retreat just completely messed up the entire order. I mean, we had 50 executives flying in from all over the coast, and they served room-temperature egg salad. In July! Who serves egg salad in the middle of summer? The smell in that conference room was just... it gets into the upholstery, you know? Those heavy velvet chairs they have at the Marriott. I told my assistant—well, my former assistant, I had to let her go because she couldn't even format a pivot table without having a meltdown—I specifically told her to book the Hyatt. But she insisted the Marriott gave us a better group rate. A better rate for spoiled mayonnaise! It's just incredible how hard it is to find competent staff these days. You give them one simple task, just one, and suddenly it's a whole production about vendor relations. I had to call the catering manager myself while I was waiting for my car in valet...

Over these past three months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or full of energy, or times when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things—separate from the voices themselves?

Depressed? Or, what did you say, unusually high energy? No, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is just... normal. I mean, I have energy, but you have to when you're running a company. You can't just sit around. 

But speaking of energy, the electricity bill for the new corporate office has been absolutely astronomical because they installed those awful, blinding LED panels on the entire executive floor. It's like working inside a refrigerator. I specifically told the facilities manager—Gary, who always wears these cheap, shiny suits that look like they're made of plastic—I told him we needed warm lighting. Sconces! But he went with the lowest bidder. 

Which is exactly what happened when we tried to repave the executive parking lot last fall. They used this terrible sealant that never fully dried, so everyone was tracking black tar onto the new lobby carpets. Do you know how much it costs to deep-clean custom wool carpeting? It's ridiculous. I had to threaten to withhold payment from the paving company, and their lawyers sent me this incredibly rude letter on a Saturday. Who sends legal threats on the weekend? It completely ruined my brunch at the country club. They were serving these miniature quiches, but the pastry was entirely too soggy on the bottom... anyway, no, my mood has been perfectly fine.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or medications—like stimulants—around the time these voices started three months ago?

Alcohol or drugs? No, no, I don't use anything like that. I don't even have time for a drink most evenings, to be honest. I might have a glass of wine at a gala, but that's it. No medications either, nothing like that. 

But speaking of galas, the annual charity dinner we hosted last month was an absolute disaster. The event planner—this woman named Beatrice who insisted on wearing these massive, clanking silver bracelets that just made noise every time she pointed at something—she completely botched the seating chart. She put the VP of Marketing right next to the head of HR, and they haven't spoken since the whole debacle with the holiday party bonus structure. It was so incredibly tense. I was sitting there trying to eat my filet mignon, which was completely overcooked, by the way. You ask for medium-rare, and they give you a hockey puck. I don't understand why it's so difficult for a five-star hotel kitchen to temperature-check their meat. 

I actually had to go back into the kitchen myself to speak to the head chef, and the floor back there was so slick I nearly slipped in my good heels. Do you know how hard it is to find a decent cobbler these days? The guy I used to go to on 4th Street retired and moved to Florida, and the new place just slaps glue on everything. It's tragic, really, what's happened to craftsmanship. But anyway, no, I haven't been taking any drugs or anything.

Since these voices first started three months ago, have they been happening continuously, or have there been stretches of time—days or weeks—where they went away completely and you felt back to your normal self?

Continuously? Well... I mean, yes, they don't really go away. They're just always there, every day. It hasn't stopped since it started. 

Which is exactly what I said to the landscapers last week about the sprinklers at my house. They just run constantly! I woke up on Tuesday, and the entire front lawn was basically a swamp. And I have these imported Japanese maples that are incredibly sensitive to overwatering. I paid a small fortune to have them brought in because the landscape architect—who, frankly, charged way too much for a few sketches on an iPad—insisted they would tie the whole modernist aesthetic together. But now they're sitting in mud. 

And do you think I can get the landscaping company on the phone? Of course not. You call their office, and it goes straight to this automated system that sounds like it was recorded in a wind tunnel. "Press one for billing, press two for service." I pressed two, and it hung up on me! Three times! I finally had to send my assistant over there in person. Not the new one, she's useless—she can't even figure out the espresso machine in the breakroom. It's an Italian machine, yes, but it has three buttons. Three! I watched her stare at it for five minutes yesterday before she just gave up and went to Starbucks. And don't even get me started on the expense reports she submits for those coffee runs. She tried to expense a cake pop last week. A cake pop! On a corporate account! I had to sit her down and explain the difference between a client meeting expense and a personal sugar craving... but no, the voices haven't stopped at all.
Have you noticed any changes in how you're able to do your job or manage daily responsibilities at work since this all started three months ago?

Work? Well, yes, things have changed. I mean, I can't really keep up with the division anymore. I try to make the executive decisions, but I just... I can't do it reliably right now. The senior staff have actually started quietly taking over the work I used to handle. 

Which is infuriating, because they don't do it right. Take the quarterly projections—David in finance thinks he's a genius because he uses these overly complicated Excel macros, but half the time they break the spreadsheet. I told him, "David, just keep it simple," but he insists on color-coding everything in these awful pastel shades. It looks like an Easter egg hunt on a monitor. And speaking of monitors, the IT department decided to replace all our dual screens with these massive curved ones. They take up the entire desk! Where am I supposed to put my physical files? I still read physical files, you know. You can't trust the cloud. Do you remember when that massive server farm went down last year and half the East Coast couldn't access their email for six hours? People were acting like it was the apocalypse. I actually had to send a courier across town with a physical contract because the digital signature platform was down. The courier was this kid on a bicycle who looked like he hadn't slept in three days, and he had the nerve to ask me for a tip before he even left the lobby. I mean, tipping culture has just gotten completely out of hand. You buy a muffin at a bakery and the screen spins around asking for twenty percent. For handing me a muffin! 

But anyway, yeah, work is... it's slipping. And at home, too. My husband has had to take over basically all the household stuff. I just leave things unfinished, or I don't even start them.
